entries.label: ex:catalogue-round-sphere
entries.title: Round shrinking spheres
entries.caption: The normalized sphere in R3 has radius 2. This is the n=2 member of the family.
entries.alt: Round shrinking spheres. The normalized sphere in R3 has radius 2. This is the n=2 member of the family.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-round-cylinder
entries.title: Generalized shrinking cylinders
entries.caption: The R3 cylinder has radius sqrt(2). Only a finite axial window is displayed; there are no end caps.
entries.alt: Generalized shrinking cylinders. The R3 cylinder has radius sqrt(2). Only a finite axial window is displayed; there are no end caps.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-plane-shrinker
entries.title: Planes through the shrinker center
entries.caption: A finite viewing patch of a plane through the origin. Its visible boundary is not part of the complete solution.
entries.alt: Planes through the shrinker center. A finite viewing patch of a plane through the origin. Its visible boundary is not part of the complete solution.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-abresch-langer
entries.title: Abresch--Langer closed shrinking curves
entries.caption: Choose m (turning number) and ℓ (curvature periods) to compute a numerical Abresch–Langer curve. The support function solves h″+h=2/h with period 2πm/ℓ. The fixed drawing and print version show (2, 3). Numerical closing gaps are diagnostics, not certified error bounds.
entries.alt: Numerical Abresch–Langer closed planar curve, initially with turning number 2 and three curvature periods. Controls allow other admissible coprime indices.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-angenent-torus
entries.title: Angenent's shrinking torus
entries.caption: A closed rotational shrinking profile in R3, with outer radius approximately 3.31470827 and inner radius 0.43712397. Return position and angle residuals before mesh rounding are below 1e-9. Numerical closure does not prove existence or uniqueness.
entries.alt: Angenent's shrinking torus. A closed rotational shrinking profile in R3, with outer radius approximately 3.31470827 and inner radius 0.43712397. Return position and angle residuals before mesh rounding are below 1e-9. Numerical closure does not prove existence or uniqueness.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-drugan-sphere
entries.title: Drugan's immersed shrinking spheres
entries.caption: Numerical shooting from pole height b ≈ 0.39345656, reflected at radius ≈ 0.83684239, in R3 with Hvec = −Xperp/2. Blue and orange distinguish the two reflected halves. Use Meridian to see the crossings or change the revolution angle to reveal interior sheets. Cut edges are display boundaries. Numerical diagnostics are not certified error bounds or a uniqueness proof.
entries.alt: Numerically integrated Drugan immersed shrinking sphere. A meridian with self-intersections is revolved about the z-axis; a 270-degree cutaway exposes the sheets.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-clifford-torus
entries.title: The Clifford shrinking torus in four-space
entries.status: Exact R4 geometry, projected to R3
entries.caption: A linear projection of the Clifford torus. The 4D rotation control changes the projection by rotating the second and fourth coordinates. Projected overlaps are not self-intersections of the embedded torus in R4.
entries.alt: The Clifford shrinking torus in four-space. A linear projection of the Clifford torus. The 4D rotation control changes the projection by rotating the second and fourth coordinates. Projected overlaps are not self-intersections of the embedded torus in R4.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-curve-products
entries.title: Products of closed shrinking curves
entries.caption: The product lives in R^(2m). The nonround curve is a numerical Abresch–Langer profile; the product construction is exact once its factors are fixed.
entries.alt: Products of closed shrinking curves. The product lives in R^(2m). The nonround curve is a numerical Abresch–Langer profile; the product construction is exact once its factors are fixed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-spherical-minimal
entries.title: Higher-codimension spherical shrinkers
entries.caption: The spherical product formula is exact. This shows its factors and ambient dimensions rather than an embedding of a higher-dimensional product in R3.
entries.alt: Higher-codimension spherical shrinkers. The spherical product formula is exact. This shows its factors and ambient dimensions rather than an embedding of a higher-dimensional product in R3.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-moller-genus
entries.title: Møller closed shrinkers of large even genus
entries.caption: Sphere of radius 2 (gold) and non-circular shrinking torus (blue, numerical ODE), following Møller’s Figures 1–2. Dashed red circles mark the intersections and are drawn through the surfaces. Rotate, zoom, toggle the sheets or cutaway, and inspect the meridian. This is the singular input before handle insertion, not a computed finite-genus shrinker.
entries.alt: Møller sphere–torus gluing input: a shaded limiting configuration and meridian show the radius-two sphere, numerical shrinking torus, and two intersection circles. No desingularized surface is computed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-grim-reaper
entries.title: The grim reaper and its cylinders
entries.caption: Exact formula on a truncated strip. Infinite vertical ends are clipped for display.
entries.alt: The grim reaper and its cylinders. Exact formula on a truncated strip. Infinite vertical ends are clipped for display.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-tilted-grim-reaper
entries.title: Tilted grim-reaper cylinders
entries.caption: Exact tilted grim-reaper formula, with the infinite ends clipped. The displayed tilt parameter is a = 0.65.
entries.alt: Tilted grim-reaper cylinders. Exact tilted grim-reaper formula, with the infinite ends clipped.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-bowl-translator
entries.title: The rotational bowl translator
entries.caption: Numerical integration of the bowl ODE, revolved about its axis; not an exact paraboloid.
entries.alt: The rotational bowl translator. Numerical integration of the bowl ODE, revolved about its axis; not an exact paraboloid.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-translating-catenoid
entries.title: Rotational translating catenoids
entries.caption: Numerical meridian ODE revolved about the translation axis. Both infinite ends are truncated. The displayed neck radius is 1.
entries.alt: Rotational translating catenoids. Numerical meridian ODE revolved about the translation axis. Both infinite ends are truncated.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-delta-wing
entries.title: Strictly convex delta-wing translators
entries.caption: Graph domain and the two limiting tilted grim-reaper cylinders. The delta-wing itself is not numerically solved here.
entries.alt: Strictly convex delta-wing translators. Graph domain and the two limiting tilted grim-reaper cylinders. The delta-wing itself is not numerically solved here.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-wang-entire-translators
entries.title: Nonrotational entire convex translators
entries.caption: Schematic of anisotropy and the quadratic blow-down in a lower-dimensional slice; not an exact translator.
entries.alt: Nonrotational entire convex translators. Schematic of anisotropy and the quadratic blow-down in a lower-dimensional slice; not an exact translator.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-prescribed-apex-translators
entries.title: Translators with prescribed apex curvatures
entries.caption: Quadratic tangent model determined by the apex Hessian. It is neither a global formula nor a solved translator.
entries.alt: Translators with prescribed apex curvatures. Quadratic tangent model determined by the apex Hessian. It is neither a global formula nor a solved translator.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-scherkenoids
entries.title: Scherkenoid translators
entries.caption: Upward convention: one plane at negative height and a periodic array at positive height. Schematic end arrangement only.
entries.alt: Scherkenoid translators. Upward convention: one plane at negative height and a periodic array at positive height. Schematic end arrangement only.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-pitchfork
entries.title: The pitchfork translator
entries.caption: One lower asymptotic plane and three upper parallel planes for upward translation; schematic, not a four-end topological model.
entries.alt: The pitchfork translator. One lower asymptotic plane and three upper parallel planes for upward translation; schematic, not a four-end topological model.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-nguyen-tridents
entries.title: Nguyen translating tridents
entries.caption: Input grim cylinder and plane, with periodic connector locations indicated. This intersecting configuration is not the exact smooth trident.
entries.alt: Nguyen translating tridents. Input grim cylinder and plane, with periodic connector locations indicated. This intersecting configuration is not the exact smooth trident.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-finite-genus-translators
entries.title: Finite-genus translators with three ends
entries.caption: Singular bowl–catenoid input and the circle to be desingularized; not an exact smooth finite-genus translator.
entries.alt: Finite-genus translators with three ends. Singular bowl–catenoid input and the circle to be desingularized; not an exact smooth finite-genus translator.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-expanding-corners
entries.title: Expanding smoothings of planar corners
entries.caption: The even time-one profile has tip height 1 and is integrated over |x| <= 6. Its asymptotic cone slope is determined by the ODE, not prescribed independently.
entries.alt: Expanding smoothings of planar corners. The even time-one profile has tip height 1 and is integrated over |x| <= 6. Its asymptotic cone slope is determined by the ODE, not prescribed independently.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-rotational-expanders
entries.title: Rotational graphical expanders over round cones
entries.caption: The R3 time-one profile has tip height 1 and is displayed up to radius 6. Its asymptotic cone is determined by this initial value.
entries.alt: Rotational graphical expanders over round cones. The R3 time-one profile has tip height 1 and is displayed up to radius 6. Its asymptotic cone is determined by this initial value.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-two-sheet-expanders
entries.title: Two-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones
entries.caption: Two reflected rotational graphical sheets with tip heights +1 and -1. The sheets share a double cone at infinity and are truncated at radius 6.
entries.alt: Two-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones. Two reflected rotational graphical sheets with tip heights +1 and -1. The sheets share a double cone at infinity and are truncated at radius 6.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-one-sheet-expanders
entries.title: One-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones
entries.caption: Connected rotational expander with neck radius 0.8, shown in the axial window [-5,5]. The drawing makes no claim about a numerically estimated critical cone angle.
entries.alt: One-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones. Connected rotational expander with neck radius 0.8, shown in the axial window [-5,5]. The drawing makes no claim about a numerically estimated critical cone angle.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-mean-convex-expanders
entries.title: One-sided expanders from mean-convex cones
entries.caption: The cone, chosen side, and homothetic leaves illustrate the theorem. No explicit general-cone expander has been computed.
entries.alt: One-sided expanders from mean-convex cones. The cone, chosen side, and homothetic leaves illustrate the theorem. No explicit general-cone expander has been computed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-expanding-networks
entries.title: Self-expanding planar tree networks
entries.caption: A tree and a 120-degree junction condition. Curved arms are not asserted to solve the expander equation. The balanced straight Y is stationary.
entries.alt: Self-expanding planar tree networks. A tree and a 120-degree junction condition. Curved arms are not asserted to solve the expander equation. The balanced straight Y is stationary.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-stationary-catenoid
entries.title: The catenoid as an eternal stationary flow
entries.caption: The waist radius is 1 and the finite parameter window is |s| <= 1.65. The complete stationary catenoid has two infinite ends.
entries.alt: The catenoid as an eternal stationary flow. The waist radius is 1 and the finite parameter window is |s| <= 1.65. The complete stationary catenoid has two infinite ends.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-whitney-sphere
entries.title: Mean curvature evolution of the Whitney sphere
entries.caption: The planar profile generates a Lagrangian immersed sphere in R^(2n). This is initial geometry, not its later evolution or an embedding of the sphere in R3.
entries.alt: Mean curvature evolution of the Whitney sphere. The planar profile generates a Lagrangian immersed sphere in R^(2n). This is initial geometry, not its later evolution or an embedding of the sphere in R3.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-degenerate-neckpinches
entries.title: Rotational degenerate neckpinch solutions
entries.caption: The cylinder and bowl are limiting models at different scales. The intermediate formula is an asymptotic limit, not a closed formula for the compact flow.
entries.alt: Rotational degenerate neckpinch solutions. The cylinder and bowl are limiting models at different scales. The intermediate formula is an asymptotic limit, not a closed formula for the compact flow.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-angenent-oval
entries.title: The Angenent oval as an explicit ancient flow
entries.caption: The planar ancient oval satisfies cos(x)=exp(t) cosh(y). The time slider shows finite negative times; its smooth flow exists for all t<0. The time slider uses a fixed spatial scale.
entries.alt: The Angenent oval as an explicit ancient flow. The planar ancient oval satisfies cos(x)=exp(t) cosh(y). The time slider shows finite negative times; its smooth flow exists for all t<0.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-kkm-one-end
entries.title: Kapouleas–Kleene–Møller shrinkers with one end
entries.caption: Sphere–plane gluing configuration and one conical end; this is not a solved shrinker mesh.
entries.alt: Sphere–plane gluing configuration and one conical end; this is not a solved shrinker mesh.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-drugan-nguyen-torus
entries.title: Drugan–Nguyen variational shrinking tori
entries.caption: Weighted half-plane construction of a closed geodesic; no identity with the numerical Angenent profile is assumed.
entries.alt: Weighted half-plane construction of a closed geodesic; no identity with the numerical Angenent profile is assumed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-bns-genus
entries.title: Buzano–Nguyen–Schulz shrinkers of every positive genus
entries.caption: Equivariant min-max construction; exactly one end is established only for sufficiently large genus.
entries.alt: Equivariant min-max construction; exactly one end is established only for sufficiently large genus.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ketover-doubled-plane
entries.title: Ketover self-shrinking doubled planes
entries.caption: Two conical ends and the doubled-plane limit describe the sufficiently large genus regime; the drawing is not a solved shrinker.
entries.alt: Two conical ends and the doubled-plane limit describe the sufficiently large genus regime; the drawing is not a solved shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-spherical-doubling-shrinkers
entries.title: Closed shrinkers from spherical doubling
entries.caption: Two sphere sheets joined by symbolic bridge sites. The theorem requires sufficiently large m; displayed dots do not specify a proved small-genus example.
entries.alt: Two sphere sheets joined by symbolic bridge sites. The theorem requires sufficiently large m; displayed dots do not specify a proved small-genus example.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-sun-wang-torus-translators
entries.title: Translators with an Angenent-torus end
entries.caption: Three-dimensional cross-sections of one translator end in four-space grow like √z times the input torus. The unknown correction and compact core are not computed.
entries.alt: Three-dimensional cross-sections of one translator end in four-space grow like √z times the input torus. The unknown correction and compact core are not computed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-sun-wang-sphere-doubling-translators
entries.title: Translators with high-genus spherical-doubling ends
entries.caption: High-genus shrinker cross-sections of one three-dimensional translator end in R4. Bridge sites and the asymptotic model are schematic.
entries.alt: High-genus shrinker cross-sections of one three-dimensional translator end in R4. Bridge sites and the asymptotic model are schematic.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ancient-torus-curves
entries.title: Ancient torus curves in higher codimension
entries.status: Exact R4 curve, projected to R3
entries.caption: Frequencies (1,2). The time slider numerically inverts r²+r⁸=−2t in the exact formula; the viewing scale stays fixed. Apparent crossings may result from projection.
entries.alt: Frequencies (1,2). The time slider numerically inverts r²+r⁸=−2t in the exact formula; the viewing scale stays fixed. Apparent crossings may result from projection.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-eternal-helices
entries.title: Eternal shrinking helices
entries.caption: The time slider inverts log r+r²/2=1/2−t. Only −5π/2 ≤ s ≤ 5π/2 is drawn; both infinite ends are omitted. The viewing scale stays fixed.
entries.alt: The time slider inverts log r+r²/2=1/2−t. Only −5π/2 ≤ s ≤ 5π/2 is drawn; both infinite ends are omitted. The viewing scale stays fixed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-double-plane-flow
entries.title: Immortal annuli converging to a double plane
entries.caption: Two sheets joined by a rotational neck; this is an unsolved schematic. Multiplicity-two convergence is local and occurs only as t tends to infinity.
entries.alt: Two sheets joined by a rotational neck; this is an unsolved schematic. Multiplicity-two convergence is local and occurs only as t tends to infinity.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-double-sphere-flow
entries.title: Immortal compact flows converging to a double sphere
entries.caption: Orbit-space profile of a flow in Sⁿ×R, with two necks collapsing only at infinite time. This is not a Euclidean MCF surface in R3.
entries.alt: Orbit-space profile of a flow in Sⁿ×R, with two necks collapsing only at infinite time. This is not a Euclidean MCF surface in R3.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-nguyen-shrinking-saddles
entries.title: Nguyen's one-ended shrinking saddles
entries.caption: Normalized sphere of radius two intersecting a plane. The highlighted circle is replaced by a bent Scherk core. The smaller periodic wave represents the core symbolically, not a solved shrinker. For sufficiently large m the construction has genus m minus one and one conical end.
entries.alt: Normalized sphere of radius two intersecting a plane. The highlighted circle is replaced by a bent Scherk core. The smaller periodic wave represents the core symbolically, not a solved shrinker. For sufficiently large m the construction has genus m minus one and one conical end.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-angenent-torus-cylinders
entries.title: Angenent torus cylinders
entries.caption: Three slices w = −12, 0, 12 of the numerical Angenent torus × R in R4, projected into R3. Use 4D rotation to change the projection. These are selected slices of one connected three-dimensional hypersurface, not three components or its entire geometry.
entries.alt: Three selected slices of the torus-cylinder in R4, with fourth-coordinate rotation before projection.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-iw-two-ended
entries.title: Ilmanen–White two-ended shrinkers
entries.caption: Two schematic sheets connected by three neck symbols illustrate the genus-two, two-ended topology. The complete ends are conical; these flat patches are not their actual geometry. The theorem constructs every genus h at least two, with h plus one equatorial neck circles, and the large-genus limit is a double plane.
entries.alt: Two schematic sheets connected by three neck symbols illustrate the genus-two, two-ended topology. The complete ends are conical; these flat patches are not their actual geometry. The theorem constructs every genus h at least two, with h plus one equatorial neck circles, and the large-genus limit is a double plane.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-shao-zou-stacking
entries.title: Shao–Zou shrinkers with any prescribed number of ends
entries.caption: Three plane patches with symbolic bridges between consecutive layers. In the theorem the number of layers k is at least two and the number m of bridges per adjacent pair is sufficiently large depending on k. The resulting shrinker has k conical ends and genus (k minus one) times (m minus one). The actual surface and cone shapes are not computed.
entries.alt: Three plane patches with symbolic bridges between consecutive layers. In the theorem the number of layers k is at least two and the number m of bridges per adjacent pair is sufficiently large depending on k. The resulting shrinker has k conical ends and genus (k minus one) times (m minus one). The actual surface and cone shapes are not computed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-hmw-platonic-polygon
entries.title: Flow-generated Platonic and polygonal shrinkers
entries.caption: The left diagram shows the six face-center rays of a cube; the right diagram shows seven equally spaced horizontal rays. These are the sets Q avoided by the constructed shrinkers, not shrinker surfaces. Genus equals the number of rays minus one. Compactness and exact end counts are not specified generally; large regular-polygon examples are noncompact.
entries.alt: The left diagram shows the six face-center rays of a cube; the right diagram shows seven equally spaced horizontal rays. These are the sets Q avoided by the constructed shrinkers, not shrinker surfaces. Genus equals the number of rays minus one. Compactness and exact end counts are not specified generally; large regular-polygon examples are noncompact.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-hmw-one-ended
entries.title: Flow-generated sphere–plane shrinkers
entries.caption: The geometric diagram is the sphere-plane limit S squared of radius two union a plane, with symbolic horizontal symmetry lines. For each positive genus g the construction gives a shrinker, and exactly one conical end is proved for all sufficiently large g. The drawn limit is not a computed finite-genus shrinker.
entries.alt: The geometric diagram is the sphere-plane limit S squared of radius two union a plane, with symbolic horizontal symmetry lines. For each positive genus g the construction gives a shrinker, and exactly one conical end is proved for all sufficiently large g. The drawn limit is not a computed finite-genus shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-hmw-three-ended
entries.title: Flow-generated three-ended shrinkers
entries.caption: Three nearby parallel plane patches symbolize the multiplicity-three plane limit. They do not depict the actual connected shrinker or its conical ends. For sufficiently large g the construction has genus 2g and three conical ends, and converges to a multiplicity-three plane as g grows.
entries.alt: Three nearby parallel plane patches symbolize the multiplicity-three plane limit. They do not depict the actual connected shrinker or its conical ends. For sufficiently large g the construction has genus 2g and three conical ends, and converges to a multiplicity-three plane as g grows.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ketover-platonic
entries.title: Ketover shrinkers with Platonic symmetry
entries.caption: Wireframes indicate the five Platonic solids used to organize doubling sweepouts. A solid with f faces leads to a shrinker of genus f minus one. These wireframes are not shrinker meshes; compactness and the number of ends of the min-max limits remain unspecified in the construction.
entries.alt: Wireframes indicate the five Platonic solids used to organize doubling sweepouts. A solid with f faces leads to a shrinker of genus f minus one. These wireframes are not shrinker meshes; compactness and the number of ends of the min-max limits remain unspecified in the construction.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-swz-large-entropy
entries.title: Sun–Wang–Zhou shrinkers of arbitrarily large entropy
entries.caption: A qualitative increasing curve illustrates the growth of Gaussian widths with the min-max parameter k. For dimensions two through six the constructed shrinker has entropy equal to the kth width, with growth comparable to k to the power one over n plus one and Gaussian Morse index at most k. No numerical entropy values or shapes are plotted.
entries.alt: A qualitative increasing curve illustrates the growth of Gaussian widths with the min-max parameter k. For dimensions two through six the constructed shrinker has entropy equal to the kth width, with growth comparable to k to the power one over n plus one and Gaussian Morse index at most k. No numerical entropy values or shapes are plotted.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-chu-sun-genus-one
entries.title: Chu–Sun genus-one shrinkers below the shrinking doughnut
entries.caption: A generic torus icon represents the topology of the starting Drugan–Nguyen rotational shrinker T. An ancient mean curvature flow and a singular blow-up produce a genus-one shrinker Sigma of strictly lower entropy. The final box deliberately leaves compactness, ends, symmetry, and geometric shape unspecified.
entries.alt: A generic torus icon represents the topology of the starting Drugan–Nguyen rotational shrinker T. An ancient mean curvature flow and a singular blow-up produce a genus-one shrinker Sigma of strictly lower entropy. The final box deliberately leaves compactness, ends, symmetry, and geometric shape unspecified.
